To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have characterized a novel ciliopathy syndrome with mutations in WDR 19 and TEKT 1, two genes previously associated with primary ciliopathies, that we have identified the function of TEKT 1 as a new component of the motile cilium, and that we have demonstrated that TEKT 1 is a new candidate gene involved in primary ciliary dysgenesis.

we identified biallellic mutations in WDSR19 and TEKT-1 genes in a child with Mainzer-Salino syndrome and ciliary dyskinesis, and showed that TEKT-1 gene is a new candidate gene in primary ciliary dyskenesis.

we identified a child with a novel syndrome, characterized by a combination of renal, retinal, skeletal and lung involvements and mutations in two novel candidate genes for ciliopathies: WDR19 and tektin1.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the functional characterization of tekt1 as a new gene for primary cilia and ciliary motility.
the functional analysis of the gene tektin- 1 in cilia and its possible role in ciliopathies such as primary ciliary dysplasia.
the identification of novel genes involved in the pathogenesis of primary ciliary dysgenesis and with the functional characterization of tekt1.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mutations of the WDR19 and/or TEKT1 genes cause a new syndrome characterized by primary and motile dysciliary disorders, which may be classified as a new type of ciliopathy.
the TEKT1 mutation is the cause of the patient's disease, as it is the most likely cause, and that it is a new cause for primary ciliary disease.
mutations in TEKT1 are associated with ciliary motility defects and that the identified TEKT1 mutations in our case may contribute to the overall clinical picture observed.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TEKT1 mutations cause a new form of ciliopathy characterized by both primary and motility ciliary defects.
TEKT1, an uncharacterized gene, is a new candidate gene in primary ciliary dysplasia.
the identification of mutations in WDR1 and TEKT1 in a patient with MZSD and primary ciliary dysplasia (PCD) is consistent with the idea that the two ciliary diseases are related.
The main takeaway from our work is that
TEKT1 mutations are a novel cause of ciliary dyskinesis.
mutations in WDR 19 and TEKT 1 cause a ciliopathy characterized by dysfunction of both primary cilia and motile ciliary structures.
TEKT1 is a new candidate gene in primary ciliary dyskenisia.
